pass_semantics: Every mandatory item must pass. A skipped, unexecuted, truncated, sampled, or zero-comparison item is a failure.

mandatory_items.requirement: The contract names all seven installed execution graphs, their six scored families, the independent incremental candidate source and all 12 installed suffixes.
Every newer mode absent from CANN 8.1 is REQUIRES_NEW_KERNEL and cannot produce a 272-byte packet or installed suffix.
Candidate construction and scoring import no official select API, RuntimeKb, tiling bank, CSV latency, XGBoost or repository lookup.
The packet generator imports and calls no official selector and emits no baseline-dependent status; the official API is invoked only by the later paired NPU measurement stage.
Every hardware-derived ideal region reports exhaustive=true; reaching max_evaluations is a failure, never a partial success.

Every family whose exact applicability predicate is true contributes candidates and varies its mandatory geometry, packet, traversal, buffering or reduction axes; a single unchanged packet cannot pass.
AL1, BL1, FixPipe, single-core Split-K, deterministic Split-K and incremental negative boundary witnesses contribute zero candidates for that family.
The incremental route converts and independently rescores every accepted source-loop candidate, not only its original cycle winner.
Repeated generation returns identical ordered candidates, metrics, winner fields and packet digest.

After exhaustive hard legality the natural pool contains at most 256 unique candidates and 128 Pareto candidates per audited shape, selection completes within two seconds on the audit host, and exceeding a bound fails instead of truncating candidates.
Every one of the 12 dtype-valid installed dispatch suffixes has an independently generated legal witness, and the incremental source branch is covered separately.
Every emitted candidate passes CANN graph, suffix, field, alignment, task coverage, memory, reduction and L2 coverage validation.
FixPipe requires M>=aicNum*512; no 128-row substitute is accepted.
FP32 FixPipe does not inherit the FP16/BF16 transA prohibition; FP16/BF16 do.
AL1 enforces M<=16, 16<N<=320, K>=4096, K%128=0, FP32 NT and full-A L1 capacity.
BL1 enforces M>16*max(K,N), K<=256 and the documented on-the-way or FP32 VNCHW resident path.
Serial Split-K owns complete MN tasks and multiple serial K chunks; deterministic Split-K owns K partitions and validates its FP32 partial-workspace tail stride.
Incremental candidates require M<=128, matching FP16 or BF16 A/B/C types, ND layouts, NT, no bias and no head ND-to-NZ conversion; every source-loop candidate is converted.
A validator separate from validate_cann_tiling checks alignment, all local capacities, L2 coverage and dispatch suffixes for every branch witness.
Ranking uses a plan reconstructed from the exact lowered CANN fields, never the pre-lowering generic plan.
Every candidate records critical and average core cycles and ranks by the maximum-core critical path plus shared hardware roofs.
Required per-family transfer, Cube, FixPipe, Vector, atomic, workspace, reduction and synchronization components are present according to the contract.
Rates come only from the frozen Ascend910B3 hardware profile; no operator-latency fit or workload identifier affects a score.
AL1 baseK, asymmetric L1 buffering, L0C ping-pong, output route and all-launched AL1 prologue changes produce observable physical cost changes.
No retained candidate is dominated on every declared hardware objective by another candidate of the same family.
No fixed candidate quota or latency-ranked preselection discards candidates before the complete Pareto test.
The selected winner is the minimum simulated cycle candidate across every applicable installed family and incremental candidate, with deterministic non-official tie-breaking.
The selected output is exactly 272 bytes, round-trips through the installed ABI and uses a dtype-dispatched installed suffix.
Workspace and blockDim are derived from the selected graph and fields; they are not copied from an official result.
The audit output contains one row for every mandatory item, raw/unique/Pareto candidate counts per family, all rejection reasons, elapsed time and the final winner.
